significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that epidemic TSFMs contain an internal signal whose transition is localized at the independently measurable threshold R_t=1, distinguishes matched curves on opposite sides of that threshold, and causally controls growth-versus-decline forecasts; this combines a form-(iii) threshold law with a form-(ii) causal claim. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—“forecast in opposite directions” despite matched momentum—and a mechanism—the steerable “R-threshold” direction—thereby fixing what should happen across an R_t sweep and how turning-point forecasts should respond to interventions, rather than merely showing decodability. The branches are determinate and useful: failure of information beyond momentum together with failed steering would rule out this threshold mechanism as the explanation for the evaluated TSFMs, although it would not rule it out for all future models; Chronos (Ansari et al., TMLR 2024) and TimesFM (Das et al., ICML 2024) make that model class consequential, while EpiEstim (Cori et al., 2013) supplies the established measurable R_t framework. In the topic-substitution check, deleting the specific “opposite R_t side,” threshold-localization, and causal-flip claims leaves only a generic scientific-mechanism probe that would merit about 5, so the claim-specific threshold relation supports an above-median score.

reach.justification: The claim hands over several named handles: the “Threshold-Beyond-Momentum Index,” “Matched-Curve Separation Ratio,” and a steerable “R-threshold direction,” together forming a diagnostic and intervention rather than a descriptive insight. The diagnostic is ex ante because the stated action is to “require explicit mechanistic (R_t-aware) validation before any TSFM is used for epidemic policy counterfactuals,” leaving developers, benchmark authors, and public-health model auditors an action window before deployment. After recalibration on a new model, the threshold relation predicts that any genuinely mechanistic signal should switch near R_t=1 and produce opposite forecasts for matched curves, but whether the new model contains such a signal must still be rediscovered, so the audit transfers more strongly than the substantive positive finding. The asserted scope covers epidemic forecasting across general and epidemiology-aware TSFMs and multiple diseases, not foundation models generally; the topic-substitution check therefore does not preserve this score, because the ex-ante threshold audit and deployment gate disappear when the claim-specific content is removed.
